candidates.title: Polyanalytic $q$-Fock spaces and the polyanalytic $q$-Bargmann transform
candidates.abstract: We study polyanalytic $q$-Fock spaces from an operator-theoretic point of view. We compute the formal adjoint $A^*$ of the Jackson derivative $A=\overline{R}_{q}$ on the polynomials in $z,\overline{z}$ inside $L^{2}(\mathbb{C},μ_{q})$ and we show that, up to unimodular factors, a twist by the grading operator is the only modification of $A$ diagonal in the grading for which a deformed canonical relation $aa^*-λa^*a=I$ holds. The resulting second-order $q$-difference operator $a^*a$ is essentially self-adjoint on the polynomials and $q$-complex Hermite polynomials span its eigenspaces. These eigenspaces give the orthogonal decomposition of $L^{2}(\mathbb{C},μ_{q})$ into true polyanalytic $q$-Fock spaces. We determine the disk on which each of them is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space and we factor the corresponding unitary $q$-Bargmann transforms through powers of $a^*$.

candidates.title: Hamiltonian Potential Optimization for Partially Observed Stochastic Optimal Control
candidates.abstract: We develop a Hamiltonian potential optimization method for partially observed stochastic optimal control with continuous-time state dynamics and discrete-time noisy observations, including controlled sensing. Rather than solving the infinite-dimensional belief-space Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation, we optimize over parametrized potentials depending on the state variable and the available observation history. The associated Hamiltonian minimizers induce admissible continuous controls and, when observations are controlled, sensing decisions. An extended Hamiltonian incorporating a cost multiplier provides a common representation of the induced belief dynamics and running and observation costs. This construction yields a finite-dimensional optimization problem, with gradients computed by a forward simulation and a backward discrete adjoint sweep. The numerical implementation uses Gaussian beliefs represented by conditional means and covariances. For nonsmooth Hamiltonians arising from switching controls, we introduce smooth Hamiltonian approximations to enable gradient-based optimization. To assess the resulting policies, we develop belief-space information relaxation lower bounds. A

candidates.title: An asymptotic bound for Yuster's independent transversal factor conjecture
candidates.abstract: An $[r,n,1]$-graph has $r$ independent parts of size $n$, with a matching between each pair of parts. Yuster conjectured in 2021 that every such graph has a partition into independent transversals whenever $n\ge 2\lceil r/2\rceil$. We prove that there is an absolute constant $A>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $r$, this partition exists whenever $n\ge\lceil r+A r^{20/21}\rceil$. Thus $f(r)\le r+O(r^{20/21})$, where $f(r)$ is the least $n_0$ such that every $[r,n,1]$-graph has such a partition whenever $n\ge n_0$. In particular, $f(r)/r\to1$, giving an asymptotic form of the conjecture.

candidates.title: Combinatorial Dvoretzky Theory
candidates.abstract: Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be an $n$-dimensional polytope such that $P \subset B_2^n$. Let $M^*(P)$ denote its mean width, and let $N$ be the number of facets (faces of dimension $n-1$) of $P$. We prove the following two bounds: (1) If $N \leq e^n$, then \[ M^*(P) \leq 1 - \frac{c}{\log^2(\frac{N}{n})}. \] (2) For arbitrary $N$, \[ M^*(P) \leq 1 - \frac{c}{n}N^{-\frac{2}{n-1}}. \] In both bounds, $c>0$ is an absolute constant.

candidates.title: A non-zero gap for the planar Mumford-Shah convex lifting and the nonexistence of crack-tip calibrations
candidates.abstract: We prove that the convex lifting of the Mumford-Shah functional constructed through the notion of calibration introduced in [2] is not sharp in dimension two. For Dirichlet boundary data prescribed by the crack-tip function, we construct a lifted competitor whose energy is strictly lower than that of the crack-tip subgraph. Since the crack-tip minimizes the original Mumford-Shah functional, this establishes a strict gap between the infima of the original and lifted problems. As a consequence we establish that the crack-tip admits no calibration.

candidates.title: Invariance and Expressiveness: Modal Variations
candidates.comment: this is a draft for a chapter in a forthcoming handbook on Comtemporary Modal Logic
candidates.abstract: This contribution focuses on bisimulation invariance as the hallmark of modal model theory and of modal modelling. It exemplifies traditional as well as more recent ramifications \&\ extensions of classical results -- involving variant modes of bisimulation equivalence and matching modalities also beyond plain Kripke structures, and emphasising especially the technical challenges in finite model theory and other non-elementary settings. Main results to be discussed revolve about the theme of expressive completeness phenomena: beside expressive completeness under bisimulation invariance in relation to first-order background logics, in the style of van Benthem--Rosen characterisations, this also concerns maximality results under criteria form abstract model theory, in the style of Lindstroem theorems.

candidates.title: Matrix-point interpolation for positive real odd functions in one and several variables
candidates.abstract: We study the single matrix point interpolation problem for positive real matrix valued functions on the right half-plane, both in the single variable setting and in the noncommutative multivariable setting. In the single variable case, a careful analysis is done for when the solution may or must have a pole at infinity. In the multivariable setting, as the pole structure at infinity can be more complicated, we focus on the case when there is no pole at infinity. The results also yield numerical algorithms for finding a solution.

candidates.title: Sharp topological overlap in every dimension
candidates.abstract: For a positive integer $d$ let $c_d^{\mathrm{top}}$ (resp. $c_d^{\mathrm{aff}}$) be the maximum $c$ such that, for every continuous (resp. affine) map from the $n$-dimensional simplex $Δ^n$ to $\mathbb{R}^d$, some point of $\mathbb{R}^d$ lies in the images of at least $(c-o(1))\binom{n+1}{d+1}$ of the $d$-dimensional faces, as $n\to\infty$. We show that \[ c_d^{\mathrm{top}}=c_d^{\mathrm{aff}}=\frac{(d+1)!}{(d+1)^{d+1}}. \] The second equality confirms a conjecture of Bukh, Matoušek, and Nivasch, who established the upper bound. The proof was found by GPT-6 Astra, following the directions of the author.

candidates.title: Convergence of the Most Probable Transition Paths in Multiscale Systems
candidates.abstract: This paper is devoted to study the convergence behavior of the most probable transition paths in a class of multiscale stochastic dynamical systems. First, based on Euler-Lagrange equations, we establish proximity and convergence results in the space of continuous functions endowed with the supremum norm. These results compare the most probable paths of the multiscale system with those of averaged system derived from the averaging principle. Next, we utilize a variational framework and analyze the Onsager-Machlup functionals using $Γ$-convergence. Together with the equi-coercivity of the functional family, we prove the convergence of both their minima and minimizers. Specifically, we show weak convergence of the minimizers in the Cameron-Martin space $H^1$, which implies their strong convergence in $L^2$.

candidates.title: The FrontierOR Challenge: Agentic Algorithm Design for Operations Research
candidates.abstract: Operations research (OR) relies on algorithms that experts tailor to each problem: a new routing, scheduling or network design problem can take weeks of specialist work before it is solved well at scale. Large language model (LLM) agents now write, test and improve code, but whether they can design algorithms that scale to realistic instances is open: in the FrontierOR benchmark's one-shot evaluation, the strongest model matches Gurobi, with an objective within 1% of Gurobi's and no slower, on only 39% of the large instances. The FrontierOR Challenge asks teams to build agentic workflows that design, test, and improve algorithms for many optimization problems at once. Stage 1 releases 60 of the benchmark's 180 audited problems, spanning six application categories and five formulation types, in weekly rounds of 15; Stage 2 introduces new problems outside the benchmark, with unseen instances. Two tracks are ranked separately: in the Main track we run the submitted algorithms in a network-isolated sandbox with open-source dependencies only; in the Self-hosted track teams solve the instances on their own machines, with any software, within a timed window. candidates.title: The $RO(C_{p^n})$-graded Tambara functor of perfectoid THH
candidates.abstract: Let $R$ be a perfect $\mathbb F_p$-algebra or a nonzero $p$-torsionfree perfectoid ring and $p$ be an arbitrary prime number. We compute the $RO(C_{p^n})$-graded Tambara functor of $\operatorname{THH}(R;\mathbb Z_p)$ for every $n\ge0$, including all homotopy groups, products, restrictions, transfers, Weyl actions and norms. We also compute genuine cyclotomic restriction.

candidates.title: Sheetwise stationarity for stationary unions of $C^{1,α}$ graphs
candidates.abstract: We prove that stationarity of a finite union of $C^{1,α}$ graphs implies stationarity of each individual graph, in arbitrary dimension and codimension. The proof closely follows the approach of Minter and Stanbury \cite{MinterStanbury}, who also raised this question in their Remark~1.6. As in their paper, we give a proof that uses the planar frequency results of Krummel, Minter and Wickramasekera \cite{KMW26} (but avoids the centre manifold construction of that paper). We also rely on the Schauder estimates for $Q$-valued functions established in \cite{Luc26}.

candidates.title: Information-Region MPC: Non-Iterative Distributed Control of Urban Traffic Signals
candidates.comment: Submitted to the 2027 European Control Conference
candidates.abstract: Centralized model predictive control (MPC) exploits network-wide traffic information to obtain the optimal solution of the network-level control problem, but its computational burden grows rapidly with network size. Iterative distributed MPC reduces the size of local optimization problems, but requires repeated information exchange and coordination within each control update. To address these limitations, this paper proposes information-region MPC (IR-MPC), which approximates the first control input of centralized MPC using limited real-time data without iterative coordination. Based on historical traffic data, we quantify how perturbations at other intersections affect the centralized first control input of each intersection and use these couplings to construct a compact information region for every intersection. At each control update, each intersection then solves a local IR-MPC problem once using current data only from its information region. SUMO simulations on a real 28-intersection network show that IR-MPC with one processor per intersection computes its control inputs 9 times faster than centralized MPC and 15 times faster than a representative iterative decomposition-based

candidates.title: Optimal Patrol Widths in the Infinite-Corridor Barrier-Guarding Game
candidates.comment: 34 pages, 2 figures. Exact rational Python verifiers and a Lean 4 library for selected lemmas and finite certificates accompany the submission
candidates.abstract: A guard of speed at most one and capture radius $r$ patrols an infinite corridor. An intruder knows the patrol and can follow any path of speed at most $q$ from one end to the other. We determine where the maximum width permitted by straight wall runners can be guarded against all such paths. Write $W_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)$ for the supremum over patrols with bounded longitudinal excursion and $F(q)=2r\sqrt{1+(3q^2+2q-1)^{-1}}$ for the wall ceiling on $1/3 < q < 1$. A four-leg bowtie attains $F(q)$ exactly for $q_a\le q < 1$, where $0.457892036651 < q_a < 0.457892036652$. For every $1/3 < q < q_a$ the supremum is strictly smaller. As $q$ approaches $q_a$ from below, $F(q)-W_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)$ is bounded above and below by positive constant multiples of $r(q_a-q)^2$. The lower estimate controls near-optimal patrols uniformly in their period. A rescaled bowtie gives the matching upper estimate. We also prove that periodic patrols give the same supremum as bounded-excursion patrols. For $q\ge1$ the one-way optimum is $r\sqrt{4+q^{-2}}$, a transverse sweep. candidates.title: Post-Hopf structures on $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ and post-Lie bialgebras
candidates.abstract: We classify post-Hopf structures on the Drinfeld-Jimbo quantum group $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$, for $q\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ not a root of unity, proving that there are exactly three isomorphism classes. We then investigate the semiclassical limits of post-Hopf quantized universal enveloping algebras and derive a compatibility condition between the induced post-Lie product and Lie cobracket. This leads to the notion of a post-Lie bialgebra. We construct a nontrivial topological post-Hopf structure on $U_\hbar(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ and determine its semiclassical limit. For the standard Lie bialgebra structure on $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, we classify all compatible post-Lie products up to isomorphism and show that the nontrivial class admits a quantization. Finally, we formulate the general quantization problem for post-Lie bialgebras.

candidates.title: Preconditioning for quadratic matrix optimization via constraint reshaping
candidates.abstract: We study quadratic optimization over orthogonality or symplectic constraints, a problem arising in eigenvalue computation, subspace analysis, and reduced-order modeling. Ill-conditioned problems have a wide positive Hessian spectrum at a minimizer, which slows first-order Riemannian methods. Existing preconditioned-metric approaches choose a Riemannian metric, which determines the resulting Hessian spectrum. We instead redesign the problem itself to find the narrowest possible spectrum. We reshape the constraints into equivalent formulations that preserve the optimal value and the solution set, giving a family of preconditioned problems parametrized by positive constraint weights. We derive a closed form for the positive Hessian spectrum in terms of these weights. Minimizing the condition number then reduces to a linear program (LP) in the logarithms of the weights. The LP attains a globally optimal design within the paired equal-block family, and its strong duality gives matching lower bounds on the condition number. candidates.title: On the dimension of $V$-variable fractals
candidates.abstract: Random recursive sets have been used to model a wide range of fractal phenomena, but they can be slow and difficult to generate. $V$-variability address this problem by allowing these sets at most $V$ distinct shapes at each level of magnification. The formulae for the almost sure Hausdorff dimension of both classes is known, and it has been conjectured that (under mild assumptions) the $V$-variable dimension converges to the random recursive dimension as $V\to\infty$. We prove this conjecture.

candidates.title: Critical nonlocal GJMS operator on odd dimensional spheres and mean field equation
candidates.abstract: For a smooth axially symmetric function on $\mathbb{S}^n$ with $n\geq 1$, in odd dimensions we prove a neat formula for the critical nonlocal GJMS operator $P_n$ similar to the one in even dimensions. With this formula, we give a simple proof of the Liouville theorem by Gui-Hu-Xie (J. Funct. Anal. 2022): Every smooth axially symmetric solution to $$\frac{1}{n+1} P_n u = (n-1)!(e^{nu}-1) \quad \mathrm{on} \quad \mathbb{S}^n,n\geq 2$$ is identically zero, without using any delicate property of Gegenbauer polynomials.

candidates.title: Moduli spaces of $(3,6)$-$K3$ surfaces and cubic surfaces
candidates.abstract: We compare the ball quotient for marked nodal cubic surfaces with the arithmetic quotient of a domain of type IV associated with $K3$ surfaces arising from configurations of six lines in $\mathbb{P}^2$. Using the Coble map and the period mapping associated with the hypergeometric system of type $(3,6)$, we identify a common open subset of the GIT quotient of six ordered points in $\mathbb{P}^2$ and the ball quotient. This identification gives an analog in dimension four of the Janus-like phenomenon for the Segre cubic and the Igusa quartic, making precise a comparison suggested by Allcock, Carlson, and Toledo. For a related family of lattice-polarized $K3$ surfaces, we give a geometric realization of the ring of meromorphic modular forms with prescribed poles and trivial character and describe the corresponding Looijenga compactification.

candidates.title: Uniform Bounds of $F$-Signature and Effective Ideal Containments
candidates.abstract: We establish inequalities between numerical invariants and ideal containments in local rings containing a field. We prove the positivity of $F$-signature for klt-type algebras essentially of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$ under prime characteristic reduction and resolve the Uniform Symbolic Topology Problem effectively for both $F$-finite strongly $F$-regular rings of prime characteristic and klt type algebras over $\mathbb{C}$. Consequently, letting $s(R)$ denote the $F$-signature and $d$ the Krull dimension, if $d\geq 2$ then $I^{\left(\left\lceil\frac{d-1}{s(R)}\right\rceil n\right)} \subseteq \overline{I^{n}}$ and $I^{\left(d\left\lceil\frac{d-1}{s(R)}\right\rceil n\right)} \subseteq I^n$ for every ideal $I \subseteq R$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$ in these settings.

candidates.title: A One-Sided Liouville Theorem and a Critical Sparse-Support Inverse Theorem for Discrete Harmonic Functions
candidates.abstract: We answer the one-sided Liouville question of Buhovsky, Logunov, Malinnikova, and Sodin (Duke Math. J. 171 (2022), Remark 1.4). There is an absolute $\varepsilon>0$ such that a real harmonic function on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ is constant if it is nonnegative on at least a $1-\varepsilon$ proportion of every sufficiently large centered square. More generally, for every nonconstant real harmonic function and every $a\le b$, the sets $\{u<a\}$ and $\{u>b\}$ each occupy a fixed positive proportion of the same arbitrarily large centered squares. Turning from sign conditions to sparse supports, we prove in three dimensions a local inverse theorem at the critical quadratic support scale. Write $Q_R=[-R,R]^3\cap\mathbb{Z}^3$. If a complex-valued function is harmonic in $Q_{30R}$ and has at most $AR^2$ nonzero values there, its support in $Q_R$ lies in at most $K_A$ characteristic planes $x_i\pm x_j=c$. The minimum number $m_3(N)$ of nonzero values in $Q_N$ among whole-lattice harmonic functions nonzero at the origin satisfies $m_3(N)=(1+o(1))(2N+1)^2$. candidates.title: Partitioned iterative FD-SPH for fluid-rigid-body interaction: Stability and validation for lightweight floating bodies
candidates.abstract: This study assesses partitioned iterative fictitious-domain smoothed particle hydrodynamics (FD-SPH) for free-surface fluid-rigid-body interaction. Extending a strong-coupling framework for deformable structures, it combines volume-based hydrodynamic loads with Newton-Euler rigid-body updates. Within each time step, the mismatch between pressure-projected fictitious-fluid and rigid-body velocities is fed back iteratively. A fractional-step interpretation identifies conditions under which Passively Moving Solid (PMS) projection and Newton-Euler updates yield identical rigid-body velocities. Single-pass and iterative FD-SPH are compared under matched conditions. A two-dimensional settling-disk benchmark agrees with published results. In three-dimensional buoyancy-driven cube tests, single-pass coupling becomes unstable at specific gravities of 0.1 and 0.2. At 0.1, reducing the time-step size by a factor of 500 does not suppress the instability. Iterative strong coupling remains stable across the tested range of 0.1-1.0. candidates.title: Time-independent equivalent matrix representation for time-domain boundary element analysis of large-scale 3D acoustic problems
candidates.abstract: This paper proposes a time-independent equivalent matrix representation for large-scale three-dimensional (3D) acoustic analysis with the time-domain boundary element method (TDBEM). In conventional TDBEM, pair-dependent retarded times couple spatial interactions to historical boundary data, causing substantial storage and history-convolution costs. The proposed representation decouples compressible spatial interactions from propagation history, allowing reuse of the same compressed spatial representation across propagation delays and throughout time marching without additional temporal interpolation of the kernel. For conventional space-time discretizations, blockwise low-rank compression yields the compressed equivalent matrix method in the $\mathcal{H}$-matrix format (CEM-$\mathcal{H}$), with dynamic cluster-pair tracking to skip inactive interactions during wavefront propagation. For low-frequency, long-wavelength problems with a bounded number of nonzero time-lag matrices, the framework is extended to the $\mathcal{H}^2$-matrix format (CEM-$\mathcal{H}^2$) using delay-consistent partitioning, shared coupling matrices, and nested cluster bases. candidates.title: Scaling limits for products of induced symplectic Ginibre matrices
candidates.abstract: We study the local eigenvalue correlations of products of independent induced symplectic Ginibre matrices in the large-dimensional limit. We establish the scaling limits of the correlation functions in the bulk, at the spectral edges, and outside the limiting spectral support, both near and away from the real axis. At regular spectral points, we show that the limiting correlations coincide with those of a single symplectic Ginibre ensemble, exhibiting Pfaffian structures near the real axis and determinantal structures away from it. At the origin, where the limiting spectral density develops a singularity, we derive an integral representation of the parameter-dependent limiting Pfaffian prekernel. Our proofs are based on a unified approach involving a differential equation for the skew prekernels and their asymptotics.

candidates.title: X Hedging: towards an eXplainable artificial intelligence option Hedging framework
candidates.abstract: We propose X Hedging, an alternative to the Deep Hedging framework that addresses computational and explainability limitations of neural-network-based hedging strategies. Deep Hedging leverages neural networks to learn flexible hedging policies but relies on opaque models and typically requires large training datasets, which can complicate interpretation and limit its effectiveness in data-constrained settings. X Hedging takes a step toward addressing these limitations by replacing neural networks with tree ensemble methods, specifically LightGBM, to estimate hedging strategies. This design provides a computationally efficient alternative while preserving strong hedging performance and moving toward more user-centered explainability. To integrate LightGBM into a reinforcement-learning-style hedging framework, we introduce an optimization approach that sequentially trains tree-ensemble models while introducing stochasticity through random training orders. In controlled experiments, X Hedging achieves performance comparable to Deep Hedging while offering greater user-centered explainability, improved computational efficiency, and substantially higher robustness when training data are

candidates.title: Full Rank and Stable Sampling of $\tanh$ Networks
candidates.abstract: We study the recovery of feedforward $\tanh$ networks of fixed architecture with $P$ parameters from finitely many point evaluations. First, we characterize the set of parameters where the differential of the realization map has full rank and show that it coincides with the regular parameters in the sense of Vla{č}i{ć} and B{ö}lcskei (2021). Second, we make use of this characterization to prove that almost every tuple of $2P+1$ sampling points yields uniform-norm Lipschitz stability on compact subsets of this parameter set. Third, we prove that for exact observations, projected gradient descent and projected Gauss--Newton converge locally from sufficiently close feasible initial guesses. The same evaluations also determine the realized function for arbitrary parameters and identify parameters in the characterized set up to permutations and sign changes of hidden neurons. Finally, we develop a general framework for real-analytic networks that highlights the role of full rank in stability and local reconstruction.

candidates.title: Inference in High-Dimensional Linear Mediation Models
candidates.abstract: Mediation analysis plays an important role in psychology, epidemiology, and genomics. Al- though high-dimensional mediation has been studied extensively, existing inferential methods typically rely on sparsity assumptions that may be difficult to justify when many individually weak mediators collectively produce a substantial effect. We study inference for both the over- all indirect effect and the effect transmitted through an individual mediator in a proportional high-dimensional regime, where the number of mediators and the sample size grow at compa- rable rates, without imposing sparsity on the mediator effects. Standard debiasing procedures for high-dimensional inference commonly rely on design-covariance information or additional structural assumptions on precision-matrix directions. In mediation models, however, the full outcome-design covariance depends on unknown mediator-model coefficients, creating an addi- tional challenge when such information or structure is unavailable. To address this challenge, we introduce an approximate debiasing procedure based on partial ridge regression and show that the resulting estimator is asymptotically bias-corrected and Gaussian. candidates.title: A note on the learning coefficient of exceptional singularities
candidates.comment: 9 pages. Builds on arXiv:2606.18440. Comments welcome!
candidates.abstract: We compute the learning coefficient of a polynomial neural network at a point of its neurovariety all of whose real parameters are good, and show that it equals $d/2$, with multiplicity one, where $d$ is the difference between the dimension of the parameter space and the dimension of the group of symmetries of the architecture. This is the value attained at a generic point of the neurovariety; consequently, exceptional singularities are invisible to the pair $(λ,θ)$ whenever all real parameters in their fibre are good. By contrast, at a full parameter in the interior of the parameter domain whose differential has non-maximal rank we show that $λ<d/2$. The two statements together give a statistical reading of the geometric distinction between nodes and cusps.

candidates.title: Computational trust as intuitionistic knowledge
candidates.abstract: In this paper, we will argue that the notion of computational trust can be understood as a form of fallible intuitionistic knowledge grounded in verification. This approach naturally captures a key aspect of trust: it involves vulnerability. Specifically, it validates the principle that verification leads to trust but does not validate the opposite principle that trust leads to verification. Thus, we can trust on good grounds that some program will perform according to its specification but the program might still fail. We present a simple logic for capturing this notion of computational trust based on constructive modal propositional logic extended with a trust modality, which will be specified in an inferential fashion and by utilizing the proofs-as-programs correspondence.

candidates.title: Coxeter Group Symmetries of Frieze Patterns
candidates.abstract: Coxeter group symmetries of frieze patterns are investigated through their relation to $2\times n$ matrices and the associated Plücker coordinates. For odd order $n$, the symmetric group acts on the set of friezes, while for even $n$, the dihedral subgroup acts. We further show that a larger group acts when $n = 6$.

candidates.title: Block decimation and perfect actions for $p$-adic valued path integrals
candidates.abstract: In earlier work we introduced a finite-partition propagator for $\mathbb{C}_p$-valued wave functions, in which the intermediate positions are integrated against atomic measures. The iterated integral evaluates the action on the equally spaced chain between the endpoints, so each partition level is obtained by iterating an exact, tree-level block decimation of two-point lattice actions, with no integration over fluctuations. This kinematic decimation is the Fréchet derivative, at the free actions, of the variational decimation underlying classical perfect actions. Since the time step $p^n$ is small in the real norm exactly when it is large $p$-adically, refinement and coarsening (the ultraviolet and infrared directions over $\mathbb{R}$) exchange roles, and each yields one limit. Under refinement, potentials supported on $\mathbb{Z}_p$, given there by a convergent power series, and entering the slice action without the time-step weight produce an interaction that stabilizes off the diagonal after finitely many steps and converges uniformly on $\mathbb{Z}_p^2$, with sharp error $p^{-M}$ after $M$ steps, to a scale-covariant (perfect) action, governed near the diagonal by a Volkenborn

candidates.title: Beyond geometric lattices: pseudo-atoms and redundant join representations in the face lattice of the permutohedron
candidates.abstract: We study the lattice obtained from the poset of ordered set partitions (the Fubini poset), ordered by merging adjacent blocks, by adjoining a bottom element of rank -1. It is the face lattice of the permutohedron. We look at it from the point of view of geometric lattices: it is graded, atomic and coatomic in the strong sense that every element is a meet of coatoms, but it is not semimodular. Its atoms are the $n!$ permutations, and its elements of rank one, which we call pseudo-atoms, are the edges of the permutohedron. Describing ordered set partitions by chains of subsets, the cuts, we show that the rank is modular whenever the meet is above $\bot$, while the join of two distant atoms can have large rank, so that the rank of the join is a metric on permutations. An element has a unique representation as a join of atoms only up to rank one; above it, irredundant representations have sizes ranging from two to the rank, and the redundancy of an element is its number of atoms minus two. candidates.title: Fourier bases for square-order Paley graphs
candidates.abstract: Let $q$ be an odd prime power and consider the Paley graph $P(q^2)$ on the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. A well-known optimal eigenfunction of this graph is supported on the norm-one subgroup, where it takes the values $1$ and $-1$ on the two cosets of its subgroup of index two. Its support has the minimum possible size $q+1$. Starting from this eigenfunction, we construct a family of multiplicative translates and prove that they form a basis of the space of complex-valued functions on $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}^{\times}$. After extending these functions to the whole field, the translates indexed by squares form a basis of one nonprincipal eigenspace of the Paley graph, while those indexed by nonsquares form a basis of the other. In particular, both nonprincipal eigenspaces admit bases consisting entirely of optimal eigenfunctions. The main ingredient is a multiplicative Fourier analysis of the shifted eigenfunction. We determine the moduli of all its Fourier coefficients and, in particular, show that none of them vanishes.

candidates.title: Safeguarded Learning-Assisted Nonlinear Conjugate Gradient Methods
candidates.abstract: A learning-assisted framework for Nonlinear Conjugate Gradient (NCG) methods is developed in which lightweight online prediction is used to support, rather than replace, the classical optimization process. The proposed approach retains the standard two-term NCG structure and introduces two independent online extreme learning machine models. The first model predicts an NCG coefficient during restart recovery or when persistent stagnation is detected, whereas the second model is used only after a line-search failure in finite precision arithmetic to propose a bounded correction to the deterministic fallback step size. Neural predictions are accepted only when they satisfy deterministic numerical safeguards, including descent, scale, and out-of-distribution requirements; otherwise, the corresponding deterministic recovery or fallback mechanism is retained. Both learning models are updated online using quantities already generated along the optimization trajectory and therefore require no additional function or gradient evaluations for training. These learning frameworks are applied to six well-known classical NCG methods, producing corresponding low-storage learning-assisted variants

candidates.title: Rigidity of ordinal spaces
candidates.abstract: A Hausdorff space $Y$ is called rigid if, for every positive integer $k$, every continuous open $k$-to-one map $p:X\to Y$ from a Hausdorff space $X$ admits a partition of $X$ into $k$ open sets, each mapped homeomorphically onto $Y$. We show that the Sorgenfrey plane is not rigid, giving negative answers in $\mathsf{ZFC}$ to Velichko's questions on finite products of rigid spaces and on strongly zero-dimensional spaces. For ordinal spaces, we prove in $\mathsf{ZF}$ that every regular uncountable cardinal with the tree property is rigid. In $\mathsf{ZFC}$, we obtain a characterization for arbitrary limit ordinals: a limit ordinal $α$ is rigid if and only if every coherent family $\langle f_ξ:ξ<α\rangle$, where $f_ξ:ξ\to\{0,1\}$, admits a uniformization. As a consequence, a limit ordinal is rigid if and only if its cofinality is rigid. The characterization also implies that $ω_1$ is not rigid in $\mathsf{ZFC}$, answering a question of Velichko.

candidates.title: Propagation of chaos with singular potentials: A weighted duality approach
candidates.abstract: We establish the propagation of chaos and derive the Vlasov equation from a many-body $N$-particle system in the mean-field regime with singular interaction forces bounded by $|x|^{-α-1}$ for $0\le α<(d-1)/2$ in dimensions $d\ge 2$, which in particular include the full range of sub-Coulomb interactions in three dimensions as well as the Coulomb interaction in two dimensions. Our proof is based on an energy-based framework for deriving weighted uniform bounds on cumulants that builds upon the recent duality method developed by Bresch--Duerinckx--Jabin in combination with a new Morawetz-type estimate, allowing us to remove the restriction to locally square-integrable interaction force kernels and handle more singular regimes.

candidates.title: A sharp bounded bijection for tight cylindric partitions
candidates.abstract: Fix a cyclic profile of coprime rank $r$ and level $\ell$, both at least three, and an entry bound $n\ge1$. Let $d$ be the deficit from the maximum volume of a tight cylindric partition. For $d\le n\min(r,\ell)$, the one-row combinatorial $R$ matches the tight cylinders whose last slice lies inside the maximizer's last slice with the partitions of $d$ in which each part occurs fewer than $r$ times. The inverse preserves the profile and entry bound. We identify every partition missed at the next deficit. A prefix test decides whether any cylinder lies outside this sector and, if so, identifies the unique one of least deficit. This explains the leading coefficient gap in Warnaar's $Q_{n,c}$. We also determine the first correction to the vertex terms of the published bounded determinant.

candidates.title: Positive semidefiniteness of random submatrices
candidates.abstract: Given a symmetric matrix $A \in [-1,1]^{n \times n}$, we estimate the probability that a random principal submatrix, obtained by taking each index independently with probability $p$, is positive semidefinite. As a corollary, we show that $O(\varepsilon^{-1})$ indices chosen uniformly at random suffice for testing positive semidefiniteness with squared Frobenius distance threshold $\varepsilon n^2$, thus nearly matching the lower bound of Bakshi, Chepurko, and Jayaram (``Testing Positive Semi-Definiteness via Random Submatrices'', FOCS 2020). The key ingredient is a dense model lemma for positive semidefinite matrices, proved using the hyperplane separation theorem and a contraction inequality for Rademacher random variables.

candidates.title: Asymptotics of Hitchin metrics and modularity of exceptional ALG gravitational instantons
candidates.abstract: We prove asymptotic estimates for the Hitchin metrics on four-dimensional moduli spaces of parabolic $\mathrm{SL}(n,\C)$-Higgs bundles on the three-punctured sphere with flag types corresponding to the Dynkin types $E_6$, $E_7$ and $E_8$. For fixed weights in the alcove interiors and fixed scalar graded residues, the Hitchin metric converges in $C^\infty$ to the semiflat metric along the end. The decay is polynomial in general and exponential when all graded residues vanish. For every admissible parameter with weights in the closed alcoves, the moduli space with its Hitchin metric is a complete nonflat ALG gravitational instanton of order two. Extending the period calculation of Dimakis--Fredrickson--Yae to the boundary and allowing compactly supported changes of marking, we obtain every point of the normalized period domain. It follows from the ALG Torelli theorem that every ALG gravitational instanton with cone parameter $1/3$, $1/4$ or $1/6$ is isometric, up to homothety and hyperkähler rotation, to one of these moduli spaces with its Hitchin metric.

candidates.title: Invariants of subfactors associated to Petrescu's Hadamard matrices of order 7
candidates.abstract: Petrescu's sixth-root $7 \times 7$ Hadamard matrix defines an irreducible, hyperfinite subfactor $N \subset M$ with Jones index 7. It is built from the spin model commuting square obtained from the Hadamard matrix by iterating Jones' basic construction. We prove that the standard invariant of this subfactor is minimal, i.e. the higher relative commutants consists of Temperley-Lieb algebras. Thus, the principal graphs of the subfactor are the Coxeter-Dynkin graph A$_\infty$. This solves a long-standing open problem. The main new idea is a congruence for the profile of the Hadamard matrix that restricts the order of rotation on the lowest-weight spaces in Jones planar algebra description of the standard invariant. Together with a uniform trace bound, this gives bounded annular multiplicities on a subsequence, which forces the principal graph to have norm at most two. We also show that the same result holds for most Hadamard matrices in Petrescu's one-parameter family. Specifically, the associated subfactors have Temperley-Lieb standard invariant at every transcendental phase and at every algebraic phase with residue $\pm1$ at a prime above three. In each fixed degree the exceptional

candidates.title: Periods, isomonodromy, and modularity of ALG/ALG$^*$ gravitational instantons
candidates.abstract: We prove that every smooth ALG or ALG$^*$ gravitational instanton of type $A_0,A_1,A_2,D_0,D_1,D_2,D_3$ is, up to homothety and hyperkähler rotation, isometric to a rank-two wild Hitchin moduli space on $\PP^1$ with its $L^2$ metric. We compute the compact hyperkähler periods and asymptotic parameters of these moduli spaces and give explicit inverse formulas for every admissible choice of these data. For the three ALG types, global isomonodromic transport realizes the two real parameters left undetermined by the compact periods. We use a Hamiltonian variation formula and uniform comparison with the semiflat metric to apply the Torelli and uniqueness theorems.

candidates.title: Adaptive Tests of Pricing Restrictions with Observed and Latent Factors
candidates.abstract: This paper develops a high-dimensional test for asset pricing models with observed and latent factors. The null hypothesis allows the intercepts from an observed-factor regression to be nonzero, provided that they lie in the latent factor loading space. We estimate the pricing errors in three steps: regress returns on the observed factors, extract latent factors from the lagged covariance structure of the regression residuals, and regress returns on both observed and estimated latent factors. The intercept from the final regression serves as the estimated pricing error. We construct Sum and Max tests based on the estimated pricing errors to detect diffuse and concentrated alternatives, respectively, and combine them using a Cauchy procedure. Under suitable regularity conditions, we establish the joint null distribution of the component statistics, their asymptotic independence, and their power against alternative hypotheses. We also propose a residual bootstrap and establish its first-order validity. Simulation studies examine the finite-sample performance of the tests under different pricing-error patterns and factor-number choices. An application to S\&P 500 stocks illustrates th

candidates.title: Dynamics of Protected State Evolution
candidates.abstract: States with identical protected observations can admit different future interventions. Each transition specifies its successor, response increment, required initial reserve and net consumption. Composing these records in execution order distinguishes protocols with equal net consumption and different initial reserve requirements. At a fixed state, a weighted Gram operator determines the linear response ellipsoid and a quotient identifies directions attainable only through cooperation between blocks. Nonlinear systems with identical complete affine data can have incomparable finite-budget response sets. In regular charts, the first correction to quadratic minimum cost is a covariant cubic form involving the third derivative of cost and the Hessians of protection and response. At singular gates, sequential feasibility depends on the peak reserve along the path. A history-weighted operator detects responses outside the old channel's range closure. Controlled congruence characterizes exact reductions of deterministic labelled dynamics, and a two-cut value identity separates the effect of paid verification from that of subsequent action selection. On Qwen2.5-7B Base, two projected polic

candidates.title: Computing Optimal Non-stationary Policies for the Probabilistic Reach-Avoid Problems
candidates.abstract: We develop and analyze an algorithm for computing optimal non-stationary policies for probabilistic reach-avoid problems. The objective in probabilistic reach-avoid problems is to maximize the probability of reaching a goal without visiting predefined avoid states. Prior work has focused on computing optimal stationary reach-avoid policies. Stationary policies use the same action distribution whenever a given state is visited. This paper shows that stationary reach-avoid policies may be suboptimal and non-stationary policies may outperform them in reach probability by a margin arbitrarily close to one. To compute optimal non-stationary policies, we reduce the reach-avoid problem to a constrained average-reward Markov decision problem and propose an algorithm to compute lottery-based policies from a standard linear program formulation. We prove that the lottery-based policies are optimal and show that they are simple to compute, analyze, interpret, and implement. The numerical experiments confirm that the lottery-based policies can outperform state-of-the-art stationary policies even in complex domains.

candidates.title: Improved Constants in the Kautz-Singleton Construction for Probabilistic Group Testing
candidates.abstract: We consider the probabilistic nonadaptive group testing problem, in which a uniformly random defective set of size $d$ is to be identified among $N$ items using a binary test matrix. For the explicit Kautz--Singleton construction, it is known that order-optimal scaling $T=Θ(d\log N)$ for high-probability recovery can be achieved in the regime $d=Ω(\log^2 N)$. However, the leading constant in this scaling remains uncharacterized even for standard low-complexity decoders. In this work, we revisit the probabilistic analysis of this construction and improve the leading constant for the COMP decoder, as well as establishing the same bound for the DD decoder. Our approach relies on a sharper analysis of the number of distinct roots associated with the defective items, yielding tighter bounds on the decoding error probability. In particular, we show that both COMP and DD achieve vanishing average error probability with $T\le (1/\ln 2+\varepsilon)d\log N$ tests for any $\varepsilon>0$, in the admissible regime $N=q^k$ for some prime power $q = Θ(d)$ and integer $k \ge 2$. For COMP, this leading constant matches that of the random near-constant column weight design, whereas for DD, a gap re

candidates.title: DeoPC: Data-Enabled Output-Feedback Predictive Control for State Regulation
candidates.abstract: Constrained regulation of the internal state of an unknown linear system is challenging when only input-output measurements are available online. In this work, we develop a data-enabled output-feedback predictive control (DeoPC) framework for constrained state regulation using input-output data. Specifically, a data-driven state estimate is constructed from past input-output data via a subspace-based singular value decomposition. Based on this state representation, we formulate a predictive controller that directly penalizes the state and control effort while enforcing the system constraints. Under persistent excitation and initialization conditions, we establish recursive feasibility and closed-loop stability of DeoPC in both noise-free and bounded-noise settings. In addition, we show that DeoPC can be calibrated to the physical state coordinates using a few offline state measurements, or treated as a model predictive control tuning problem when no state measurements are available. The effectiveness of DeoPC is demonstrated through simulations on an unstable batch reactor system.

candidates.title: Dimension-Free Buffer Bounds for Compressed-Momentum Error Feedback
candidates.comment: Submitted to a journal and details will be confirmed once paper accepted
candidates.abstract: Analyses of error feedback bound the memory buffer through a compressor contraction constant -- $r/p$ for the best rank-$r$ approximation of a $p$-dimensional spectrum -- which survives into the rate. We show it need not appear at all. When the compressed momentum is re-injected into the pre-compression accumulator, the previous compressed momentum $β_1 M_{t-1}$ is an admissible competitor in the projection, and the buffer obeys $\|E_t\|_F \le (1-β_1)\|G_t\|_F + γ\|E_{t-1}\|_F$, free of the dimensions $m,n$ and of the rank $r$. The argument uses only that the compressor is a metric projection onto a closed cone, so it covers top-$k$ selection as well as truncated SVD, holds for every selection from the projection set with no condition on singular-value crossings, and in its trajectory-tracking form assumes nothing about the gradients. In the two-stage template of the standard analyses it replaces a Stage-2 constant of order $p^2/r^2$ by one of order $1$, against $Θ(p/r)$ for the sharpest contraction-based bounds. Transferring the full rate costs a leakage term, which we bound by the step-weighted gradient mass $\sum_{u\le t}η_u\|G_u\|_F$ and show tight up to a factor $\sqrt{2}$; th

candidates.title: Total acyclicity of Q-shaped diagrams and N-stable categories
candidates.abstract: We study total acyclicity of $\Q$-shaped diagrams of projective modules. We prove that an acyclic $\Q$-shaped diagram $P$ of projective $A$-modules is totally acyclic if and only if the associated module $K_q(P)$, or equivalently $C_q(P)$, is Gorenstein projective for every $q\in \Q$. We also establish Frobenius structures on the categories of acyclic and totally acyclic $\Q$-shaped diagrams of projective $A$-modules and introduce the associated defect category. Using adjunctions between $\Q$-shaped diagrams and chain complexes, we compare this category with the classical projective defect category and show that their vanishing is equivalent under a mild condition on the Serre functor of $\Q$. Finally, we apply our results to $N$-complexes and extend the $N$-stable equivalence of Brightbill and Miemietz beyond the Gorenstein setting, obtaining a triangle equivalence between the homotopy category of totally $N$-acyclic complexes of projective $A$-modules and the $N$-stable category of Gorenstein projective $A$-modules.

candidates.title: Interference Bounds and Merge-Aware Training Dynamics for Composable Fine-Tuned Models

candidates.abstract: Combining fine-tuned models by composing their parameter updates has become a standard alternative to multi-task training. We formalize composability as a property of a collection of task vectors and prove that the excess loss of the merged model is controlled by an interference functional of the cross-task curvature overlap and the signed alignment of the updates. In the quadratic regime this functional equals the excess loss, giving a criterion that is necessary as well as sufficient and that measures the angle between task vectors in the curvature metric rather than the Euclidean one. Fine-tuning under a curvature-guided regularizer -- constructed from curvature statistics of the kind memory-efficient optimizers maintain -- keeps displacement in the base curvature metric below a ceiling set by the penalty coefficient at every iterate, at the standard $O(1/\sqrt{T})$ non-convex rate. Under a single Loewner comparison between the base statistic and the task curvatures, this control converts into a ceiling on the interference functional, inversely proportional to the penalty coefficient, so that the curvature term of the bound is controlled during training. candidates.title: Formality of finite abelian covers and Jordan blocks of the monodromy
candidates.abstract: Let $X$ be a connected finite-type CW-complex with a map to the circle that is surjective on fundamental groups. If $X$ is formal, the algebraic monodromy of the associated infinite cyclic cover has no Jordan block of size greater than one at the eigenvalue 1, over the rationals; if the $d$-fold cyclic cover of $X$ along the map is formal, the same holds at every $d$-th root of unity. We study how formality of finite abelian covers and Jordan blocks of the monodromy constrain each other. We call $X$ Alexander formal if there are no such blocks at any root of unity, rationally, nor at the eigenvalue 1 modulo any prime $p$. Each condition amounts to the vanishing of certain Massey products along the class of the map; together they say that the rational cochains of every finite cyclic cover along the map, and the mod-$p$ cochains of $X$, are formal as DG modules over the cohomology of the circle. candidates.title: Rational Elliptic Period Relations Across Realizations: Complex Lattices, Local p-adic Periods, and Drinfeld Modules
candidates.abstract: We determine the algebraic relations among full de Rham comparison periods of elliptic curves over finite extensions of $\mathbb Q_p$. The connected local monodromy group gives the transcendence degree and an explicit affine linear relation ideal for the full matrix in Fontaine's field $B_{\mathrm{dR}}$. After normalizing the holomorphic row and reducing to $\mathbb C_p$, the transcendence degree drops by one and the normalized determinant supplies the additional relation. Every polynomial relation of degree at most $d$ is detected modulo $t^{d+1}$. For $d\ge1$ this bound is sharp for each elliptic curve. A rational quasi-period row gives a Galois-stable Tate line. Together with an algebraic holomorphic period ratio it forces potential splitting, which identifies the exact ordinary CM obstruction. We compute the full Tate matrix. For ordinary non-CM curves with $p\ge5$, the standard quasi-period row is rational precisely at a zero of Katz's $E_{2,p}$. Away from the zeros the two full ratios are algebraically independent. At the zeros, a nonzero quasi-period and the normalized holomorphic ratio have algebraically independent images in $\mathbb C_p$. The complex question that motivat

candidates.title: Dynamical edge universality and the Airy$_β$ line ensemble
candidates.abstract: We prove dynamical edge universality for three families of interacting particle systems for every $β>0$: $β$-Dyson Brownian motion with an analytic potential, weighted $β$-corners processes, and a class of discrete-time Markov chains. Our results apply to general non-equilibrium initial data and show that the Airy$_β$ line ensemble emerges at positive times whenever the limiting density has a regular square-root edge. More precisely, after centering at the moving deterministic edge and rescaling space and time on the $n^{-2/3}$ and $n^{-1/3}$ scales, respectively, the trajectories of the top $k$ particles converge jointly in distribution to the top $k$ curves of the Airy$_β$ line ensemble, for every fixed $k$, in the topology of uniform convergence on compact time intervals. The proof combines dynamical loop equations with characteristic-flow estimates to establish local laws near the moving edge and upper bounds on the extremal particle. We then identify the stochastic evolution of every subsequential limit of the rescaled Stieltjes transform and establish convergence through the pole-evolution characterization of the Airy$_β$ line ensemble.

candidates.title: Certified pandigital approximations of $π$, $γ$, $δ$ and $e$
candidates.comment: 50 pages, 1 figure. Code, data and certificates: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24356239
candidates.abstract: In 2004 Erich Friedman asked for the best approximations of $π$, $e$, the Euler-Mascheroni constant $γ$ and Feigenbaum's constant $δ$ that use each of the digits $1,\dots,n$ exactly once, with addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, exponentiation, parentheses and the decimal point. We determine the optimal expressions for $π$, $γ$ and $δ$ for every $n \le 9$, with the digits in any order and in increasing order, and for $e$ when $n \le 6$. The optima are found by exhaustive search and certified by an independent algorithm that encloses every expression rigorously and decides each candidate with Arb and exact arithmetic; a second certified computation covers intermediate values of any size. Twenty-one entries improve the published records; for $π$ with the digits 1-9 the optimal error is $2.81\cdot 10^{-14}$. For $e$, whose records come from identities between power towers, we prove that Bamberger's formula is optimal within the natural family of such identities. All code and certificates are public.

candidates.title: The Semi--Fibonacci Partition Tree
candidates.abstract: In this work, we introduce a binary tree in which every semi-Fibonacci partition appears exactly once. The left--right address of a vertex gives an explicit formula for the parts of the corresponding partition and encodes statistics such as the largest $2$-adic valuation among its parts. We construct a sign-reversing involution that refines Andrews's parity theorem by determining the difference between the numbers of partitions of a given integer at even and odd depths. Inspired by properties of the Calkin--Wilf tree, we study several parameters of our tree and use them to obtain new results on semi-Fibonacci partitions. We also derive generating functions for partition statistics and determine the average and extremal partition sizes at each level.

candidates.title: Counting Elements and Conjugacy Classes of Fixed Genus in Hyperbolic Groups
candidates.abstract: Let $G$ be a non-elementary hyperbolic group equipped with a word metric. A group element in $G$ has orientable genus $n$ if it can be written as the product of $n$ commutators and no fewer. Similarly, a group element in $G$ has non-orientable genus $m$ if it can be written as the product of $m$ squares and no fewer. We obtain the asymptotic order of growth for both the number of group elements and the number of conjugacy classes in $G$, with length at most $L$, and fixed genus (orientable or non-orientable) $n$. For free groups, our methods give precise asymptotics for each of the counts.

candidates.title: Proof Checking Continuous Reachability
candidates.abstract: This paper introduces a proof format and proof checker for certifying reachability computations of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) with polynomial vector fields. Establishing a proof checking framework for certifying ODE reachability is similar to the checking of UNSAT proofs for propositional satisfiability solving, but it is even more important due to the challenges inherent in dealing with ODEs, and even more challenging due to the numerical nature of ODE reachability algorithms. The proofs are expressed in differential dynamic logic (dL), and can be independently verified with symbolic theorem provers for dL (e.g. KeYmaeraX). Such proofs are naturally generated by reachability algorithms based on Taylor models, a popular technique to obtain rigorous bounds on approximations of ODEs. This paper proves the completeness of such proofs - if an approximation was correctly computed by some (possibly untrusted) reachability algorithm via Taylor models, then a corresponding proof in dL can be automatically generated and checked to be correct in dL's proof calculus. A dedicated proof checker is implemented in Lean4 for improved performance, which is capable of formally verifying

candidates.title: Kernel Regression using Persistence Diagrams
candidates.abstract: Persistence diagrams are widely used in topological data analysis to summarize topological and geometric structure in data. We study nonparametric regression where inputs are persistence diagrams and outputs are real-valued. Using kernel-based local averaging estimators defined directly over diagram space with Wasserstein distance, we establish consistency and derive bounds on the rate of convergence under suitable assumptions in the $L^2$-theory. We also present computational experiments that demonstrate strong performance of the proposed estimator, particularly in low data regimes.

candidates.title: Moduli of continuity preserved by the Hilbert Transform
candidates.abstract: It has long been known that the Hilbert transform preserves certain moduli of continuity such as Hölder continuity. In~\cite{GS01}, M. Goldstein and W. Schlag provided a criterion, based on two simple conditions, for a modulus of continuity to be preserved under the Hilbert transform. These conditions are not satisfied by the weak-Hölder and the log-Hölder moduli of continuity. More recently, A. Avila, Y. Last, M. Shamis and Q. Zhou proved in~\cite{ALSZ21} that for compactly supported $t$-log-Hölder continuous functions ($t>1$) their Hilbert transforms are at least $(t-1)$-log-Hölder continuous. A similar result holds for weak-Hölder continuous functions. In this note we extend these results to a class of continuous functions satisfying a couple of mild integrability conditions.

candidates.title: Integer Programming Strategies for the Snake-in-the-Box Problem
candidates.abstract: We present a selection of Integer Programming (IP) strategies for the Snake-in-the-Box problem, which asks for the longest induced path in the $d$-dimensional hypercube. Current records are based on sophisticated, exhaustive searches, with optimality proven only for instances up to dimension 8, motivating our study of IP formulations. We address symmetries and potential strengthenings. With the smallest open instance having as few as 512 binary decision variables, the proposed IPs offer a challenging and intriguing combinatorial problem. In addition, we extend the problem to higher-dimensional grid graphs and provide solutions for unexplored and unsolved instances.

candidates.title: Nilpotent skew-symmetric tridiagonal Bohemian matrices: a proof of Corless's conjecture
candidates.abstract: Corless studied the skew-symmetric tridiagonal matrices $T_m(u)$ with superdiagonal $u \in \{1, i\}^{m-1}$. He showed that $T_m(u)$ can be nilpotent only if $m = 2^K - 1$ and that the $2^{K-1}$ vectors $u$ obtained from the empty vector by repeated application of $u \mapsto (u, 1, i, \rev u)$ and $u \mapsto (u, i, 1, \rev u)$ give nilpotent matrices, and he conjectured that there are no others. We prove this conjecture. Reducing the characteristic polynomial modulo $4$ gives a necessary condition for nilpotency that is linear over $\F$. For $m > 1$ it forces $u = (v, 1, i, \rev v)$ or $u = (v, i, 1, \rev v)$, and an identity implicit in Corless's proof then reduces the problem to $v$. Since $T_m(u)$ is diagonally similar to a finite section of the Feinberg--Zee hopping matrix, the theorem also determines the nilpotent tridiagonal sign matrices. We further show that the $(1,1)$ entry of the resolvent of a nilpotent $T_m(u)$ is $λ^{-1} \pm λ^{-3} \pm λ^{-7} \pm \dots \pm λ^{-(2^K - 1)}$, with signs that determine $u$. The proof of the main theorem has been formalised in Lean~4.

candidates.title: Steinness and Complete Expanding Kähler-Ricci Solitons
candidates.abstract: We prove that complete expanding Kähler-Ricci solitons with complete soliton fields characterize Steinness of relatively compact domains in Stein manifolds, and hence pseudoconvexity of bounded domains in $\mathbb{C}^n$. We construct canonical, instantaneously complete Kähler-Ricci flows from positive closed $(1,1)$-currents with global plurisubharmonic potentials and vanishing Lelong numbers. Nonzero currents homogeneous under a complete real holomorphic flow yield nontrivial expanders with prescribed soliton fields. We obtain a product criterion and uniformization results for balls and finite-type domains in complex surfaces. If $D$ is a relatively compact Stein domain in a reduced pure-dimensional Stein space of dimension at least two and $\operatorname{Sing} D$ is finite and nonempty, we prove that $\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{Reg} D)$ is compact, excluding nontrivial expanders with complete soliton fields.

candidates.title: The Bolker condition and overdetermined FBI transforms
candidates.abstract: We study real analytic canonical relations satisfying the Bolker condition and show that, in the FBI representation, they can be described by phases of overdetermined FBI transforms. As an application, we give a simplified proof of an analytic regularity result for generalized Radon transforms due to Mazzucchelli-Salo-Tzou.

candidates.title: The rational points of the non-split Cartan modular curve of level 121
candidates.comment: 41 pages, 1 figure. Programs and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24061904
candidates.abstract: We prove that the modular curve $X_{\mathrm{ns}}^{+}(121)$ of the normalizer of a non-split Cartan subgroup of level 121, of genus 511, has exactly seven rational points, all of them CM. This is the level 121 case of a conjecture of Rouse, Sutherland and Zureick-Brown, and with their theorem it determines the 11-adic images of Galois of non-CM elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$. The Jacobian has rank equal to the genus. At $p = 17$ and $43$ one Hecke block of the Mordell-Weil group has logarithm divisible by $p^2$ but $p$-adic height of valuation one, and a comparison of valuations in the quadratic Chabauty identity then shows that each CM point is the only rational point in its residue disc, with no computation of the local height at $p$, no basis of the Mordell-Weil group and no equations for the curve. The inputs come from expansions of differentials at CM points and from a formula we prove for intersection numbers of CM divisors of coprime fundamental discriminants under Hecke operators on $X_{\mathrm{ns}}^{+}(\ell^e)$ (Theorem 1.3).

candidates.title: Iterative constructions of semifields 2-dimensional over a nucleus
candidates.abstract: The construction of finite semifields dates back to Dickson's work in 1906. To the best of our knowledge, only two iterative constructions were previously known: those of Hiramine, Matsumoto and Oyama in 1987, and of Kantor and Williams in 2004. The latter yields, for suitable even orders, superpolynomially many pairwise non-isotopic semifields. In this paper, we use skew-polynomial rings to give a new iterative construction of finite semifields. This construction produces large families of pairwise non-isotopic semifields, each of which is $2$-dimensional over one of its nuclei. In particular, we show that this construction method yields semifields not contained in any family of semifields known so far.

candidates.title: On the ring of bounded functions on the character variety
candidates.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{X}$ denote the character variety associated to the group $(o_L, +)$, where $o_L$ is the ring of integers in a finite extension $L/\mathbb{Q}_p$. $\mathfrak{X}$ is a rigid analytic variety parametrizing locally $L$-analytic characters. Let $Λ_L\left(\mathfrak{X}\right)$ denote the global sections bounded by $1$. In this paper we prove that $Λ_L\left(\mathfrak{X}\right)= o_L[[o_L]]$, answering the question posed in [AB24].

candidates.title: Small-Gain Analysis of Robust Event-Triggered Extremum Seeking for Scalar Maps
candidates.abstract: We study a sample-and-hold implementation of gradient extremum seeking for a scalar quadratic map in which the control signal is refreshed only when an event occurs. The event generator acts on the demodulated gradient signal as it is actually measured, rather than on its averaged version, and contains a strictly positive offset, following the small-gain philosophy for robust event-triggered control. Rather than invoking averaging theorems, we work directly with the exact dynamics of the parameter estimation error. In the scalar setting, the demodulated gradient has an explicit sinusoidal structure, which is exploited through a change of variables that absorbs the zero-mean oscillatory perturbation, together with a quadratic Lyapunov function and the persistence of excitation of the probing signal. For a sufficiently fast dither, the estimation error is shown to decay exponentially to a residual neighborhood of the origin whose size is quantified by the dither amplitude and frequency, and by the relative threshold and the offset of the event generator. candidates.title: Optimal Robust Community Detection
candidates.abstract: We study community detection in the sparse two-community stochastic block model when an adversary may corrupt a small constant fraction of the edges of the observed graph. For every choice of parameters above the Kesten-Stigum threshold and every $\varepsilon > 0$, we give a nearly-linear-time algorithm which estimates the communities with accuracy within $\varepsilon$ of the information-theoretically optimal accuracy, while tolerating a small constant fraction of adversarially corrupted edges. Previously, efficient algorithms with optimal accuracy were known only in the absence of corruptions, while robust algorithms either achieved only weak recovery or approached optimal accuracy only in the limit of large signal-to-noise ratio. Our algorithm is simple: approximate the second eigenvector of the nonbacktracking matrix, using a semidefinite program to cope with the corruptions, and use it to initialize belief propagation. Along the way, we show that in the absence of corruptions, belief propagation initialized at this eigenvector achieves optimal accuracy, resolving an open problem of Zdeborová in the two-community case. candidates.title: \textsc{Max-Cut} on Token Graphs
candidates.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, with a positive weight assigned to each edge. A cut of $G$ is a partition of its vertices into two sets $X$ and $Y$; the weight of $(X,Y)$ is the sum of the weight of the edges of $G$ with one endpoint in $X$ and the other endpoint in $Y$. The Max-Cut problem asks for the maximum weight, $m(G)$, of a cut of $G$. The $k$-token graph of $G$, is the graph, $F_k(G)$, whose vertices are the $k$-subsets of vertices of $G$, two of them being adjacent when their symmetric difference is an edge of $G$. The phase-reconstruction problem for Heisenberg antiferromagnets in physics can be rephrased as a Max-Cut problem on token graphs. Motivated by this, we study the Max-Cut problem on token graphs, mainly when all edges are assigned the same weight. Our main focus is to bound $m(F_k(G))$ in terms of $m(G)$. candidates.title: An α-potential linear approximation for LQ differential games
candidates.abstract: Feedback Nash equilibria of infinite-horizon linear-quadratic (LQ) differential games are characterized by coupled algebraic Riccati equations (cAREs), whose numerical solution generally relies on iterative algorithms and can be highly sensitive to their initialization. Motivated by the $α$-potential-game framework, this letter proposes an $α$-potential linear approximation for constructing a systematic, game-dependent initialization. For an N-player LQ game, a reference potential game is constructed. Its equilibrium requires solving only one standard algebraic Riccati equation. The original cAREs are subsequently linearized around this reference solution, yielding a coupled linear system whose solution provides player-specific corrections and hence an approximate feedback Nash equilibrium. The resulting approximation is used to initialize three standard cARE solvers. Numerical experiments on $10^4$ randomly generated two-player games show that the proposed initialization reduces the mean number of iterations. Further experiments for $N=2,\ldots,13$ show that the reduction in iteration count persists as the number of players increases.

For large datasets of size $N$, however, classical matrix operations incur prohibitive $\operatorname{poly}(N)$ scaling, even when extracting low-dimensional spectral features or targeted scalar observables. A common-state construction further allows the block-encoding queries to be used across multiple scalar observables. candidates.title: Detection and Recovery of Core--Periphery Structure in Random Geometric Graphs
candidates.abstract: Core--periphery (CP) structure, characterized by a dense core of interconnected nodes linked to sparsely connected peripheral nodes, is a prevalent feature of many real-world networks. We propose a core--periphery random geometric graph (CP-RGG) model in which vertices are independently and uniformly distributed on the unit cube \([0,1]^m\), and each vertex is designated as a core node with probability \(p_n\). Two vertices are connected if their Euclidean distance falls below a type-dependent threshold, governed by three distinct radii for core--core, core--periphery, and periphery--periphery pairs. We investigate the information-theoretic limits for both the detection and recovery of the core in the CP-RGG. For detection in the non-degenerate regime, we prove that the total variation distance between the CP-RGG and a null RGG without CP structure converges to one if and only if the expected number of core nodes tends to infinity. candidates.title: The Scaled Dirichlet Distribution: Lauricella Representations and Estimation
candidates.abstract: We derive explicit expressions for the mixed moments of the scaled Dirichlet distribution in terms of the Lauricella hypergeometric function of type $D$. The relationship with Carlson's multivariate $R$-function is stated, and the convergence conditions required for the series derivation are made explicit. The general expressions yield means, second moments and covariances, with Gauss and Appell hypergeometric representations in the bivariate and trivariate cases. Method-of-moments and maximum-likelihood formulations are presented, together with simulation summaries and an illustrative comparison of scaled Dirichlet and ordinary Dirichlet fits to compositional futures-return data.

candidates.title: A Modified Quasi-Newton Method for Unconstrained Optimization with Nonpositive Curvature Detection and Structured Complexity

candidates.abstract: We consider the convergence, worst-case complexity, and implementation of R2N, a modified quasi-Newton method for large-scale unconstrained smooth optimization. At each iteration, we compute a step that approximately minimizes the sum of a quadratic model of the objective with an adaptive quadratic regularization, and that results in sufficient decrease. The objective is only assumed to be $C^1$, although second derivatives may be used if they are available. The implementation features a broad range of step-computation strategies, from sparse factorization to matrix-free Krylov methods, that satisfy global convergence requirements. When detected, directions of nonpositive curvature are exploited. Our analysis allows unbounded model Hessians, provided they satisfy a mild growth condition. We derive a worst-case evaluation complexity bound that separates the progress made along positive- and nonpositive-curvature directions. By forcing the regularization parameter to vanish near isolated local minimizers, we obtain superlinear local convergence. candidates.title: The Partial Trace Functor on Soergel Bimodules in Type $\mathbb{B}$
candidates.abstract: We write down some observations about the partial trace functor between the categories of Soergel bimodules of type $\mathbb{B}_{n+1}$ and $\mathbb{B}_n$ for future reference. In particular, we observe that, like in type $\mathbb{A}$, the partial trace sends Soergel bimodules to a semi-infinite $q$-graded sum of Soergel bimodules.

candidates.title: On the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv problem for $\mathbb Z_n^3$
candidates.abstract: The Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant $\mathsf s(\mathbb Z_n^r)$ is the least positive integer $t$ such that every sequence of $t$ elements of $\mathbb Z_n^r$ contains $n$ terms whose sum is zero. In this paper, we prove that $$\mathsf s(\mathbb Z_n^3)=9n+o(n)$$ for odd $n$. For every fixed $r\ge 4$, we also show that $\mathsf s(\mathbb Z_n^r)\le\bigl(\binom{2r-1}{r}+1\bigr)n+o_r(n).$ Our approach combines Alon--Dubiner-type spectral expansion, Zakharov's convex-geometric framework, and restricted-sum ideas developed by Han and Ren.
